note: Singapore: performing as an actor, singer, dancer or musician at a public performance venue (bars, discotheques, lounges, nightclubs and other venues with a Category 1 Public Entertainment Licence excepted, unless the event is government-supported), and acting in location filming for television or film, are Work Pass Exempt activities: for any number of visits up to 90 days in all in a calendar year (taken as 90 within 365), notified to the Ministry of Manpower, each stay as long as the Short-Term Visit Pass given at entry. Beyond them a performer needs a regular work pass; the Work Permit for performing artistes has ceased.

sources.title: Ministry of Manpower, Work Pass Exempt Activities: eligible activities
sources.said: You are allowed to perform a Work Pass Exempt (WPE) activity for any number of visits, but up to a total of 90 days in a calendar year ... Involvement as an actor, model, director, member of the film crew or technical crew, or photographer for: Location filming leading to TV or movie production. ... Performing as an actor, singer, dancer or musician, or involvement as a key support staff in an event held at a public performance venue, except for bars, discotheques, lounges, nightclub, pub, hotel, private club and restaurant venues with a Category 1 Public Entertainment Licence (PEL).

sources.title: Ministry of Manpower, Work Permit for performing artiste
sources.said: The Work Permit (Performing Artiste) scheme has ceased ... MOM no longer accepts applications for this pass. Businesses can instead consider engaging entertainment service providers or hiring eligible foreigners on a regular work pass.
